newsitem.title: USA: Texas mother, accused of killing sons, goes on trial.
newsitem.headline: Texas mother, accused of killing sons, goes on trial.

text.p: A Texas woman was due to go on trial on Monday, accused of murdering two of her young sons with a knife and then slashing herself to fool police.
Darlie Routier, 27, denies allegations that she repeatedly stabbed her sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5, as they slept in the living room of their comfortable suburban home near Dallas seven months ago.
Routier said a male intruder, dressed in dark clothes and a baseball cap, broke into her home early on June 6 and killed the two boys "like an animal killing sheep" before stabbing her and escaping.
But prosecutors accused her of inventing the story about an intruder and of stabbing herself in the neck and shoulder to back up her story. They have charged her with capital murder.
Police arrested Routier 12 days after the murders, saying her oral statement was full of inconsistencies and that medical examinations showed her wounds were self-inflicted.
Her husband Darin, who was upstairs sleeping with the couple's infant son at the time of the murders, has not been charged by police and insists that his wife is innocent.
Routier says she and the two boys fell asleep while watching television and that she only woke up when the intruder attacked her.
State District Judge Mark Tolle moved the trial from Dallas to the southern Texas city of Kerrville because of intense publicity, and also put a gag order on the case.
A jury of seven women and five men was selected in mid-November.
Routier could be sentenced to death if found guilty.
Most of the trial testimony was expected to focus on blood-stained clothes, the alleged murder weapon and DNA samples taken inside and around the Routiers' home in the Dallas suburb of Rowlett.
